newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Australia-Malaysia ties not affected by racism row.
newsitem.headline: Australia-Malaysia ties not affected by racism row.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Saturday that anti-Asian remarks by a maverick politician had not affected ties between his country and Malaysia.
Downer, on a two-day visit, said Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad made this clear during their brief meeting on Friday.

"Mahathir has made his decision on this issue perfectly clear that he won't judge a country by the views of one maverick," Downer told reporters after addressing the Malaysia-Australia University Alumni Convention.
"Mahathir said to me that every country has its mavericks."

Racism and racial issues have made headlines in Australia since independent member of parliament Pauline Hanson criticised the government over the number of Asians in Australia and hinted at an Asian invasion threat.
"The remarks of a maverick like that aren't a reflection of the views of the Australian government or the broader mainstream of the Australian community," Downer said.
Hanson, in a newspaper interview, also warned that Australia faced a Bosnia-style civil war if migrants and Aborigines continued to get special treatment.
Australian trade officials and industry groups have expressed concern that the row could hurt the country's burgeoning trade ties with its neighbours in Asia.
Downer said Australia's immigration policy was and would remain non-discriminatory.
"Australia has a proud record for welcoming migrants from all around the world and we will not let that achievement be threatened," he said.
Mahathir, once sharply critical of Australian policies and manners, said at a banquet on Friday that relations between Malaysia and Australia were stronger now than before.
Ties were strained in the 1980s when then Australian Prime Minister Bob Hawke called the hanging of two convicted Australian drug traffickers by Malaysia a "barbaric" act.
Relations hit a low in 1993 after then Australian Prime Minister Paul Keating called Mahathir "recalcitrant" for skipping the inaugural Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Seattle.
Over the years, Malaysia has also expressed outrage over what it viewed as unflattering portrayals of itself in film and television presentations by Australians.
